subject: literature
passage: Once a year, Mr. Haddad drove his old van into the hills to tune the only piano in the village of San Isidro. This year, a landslide blocked the main road, and he had to take a long detour through the valley. By the time he finally reached the school, the children ______ in the courtyard for nearly two hours, and several of them ran to the gate to help him carry his heavy case of tools.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: The story is told in the past tense ("drove," "reached," "ran"). The waiting began before Mr. Haddad arrived and continued up to that past moment, which "By the time he finally reached" signals. An action that continued up to a point in the past takes the past perfect progressive, "had been waiting."
explanation.A: Incorrect. The present tense "wait" doesn't fit a story told in the past.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The present progressive "are waiting" doesn't fit a story told in the past.
explanation.C: Correct. "Had been waiting" shows that the waiting went on before and up to the past moment when he arrived.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The future perfect "will have waited" refers to the future, but the arrival already happened.
